TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Caldwell (TSX:CWL)(OTCQX:CWLPF), a leading retained executive search firm, today announced it has completed the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of its wholly owned subsidiary, IQTalent Partners, Inc., to WinMil, Inc. WinMil will continue to operate the business under the IQTalent name and brand.

Caldwell acquired IQTalent in 2020 to broaden its service offerings into technology-enabled recruiting solutions at the professional level. After nearly six years, Caldwell determined that the business was not meeting the firm's strategic objectives and that a sale would better align its portfolio with its long-term priorities.

"Divesting IQTalent enables us to sharpen our focus on what Caldwell does best: delivering elite executive search and advisory services to our clients," said Chris Beck, chief executive officer of Caldwell. "IQTalent has been an important part of our portfolio, and we are proud of the innovative team and platform we helped build. We believe the business is well-positioned to succeed under WinMil's ownership, and we look forward to continuing a collaborative relationship through our referral partnership."

Founded in 2009, IQTalent pioneered an on-demand recruiting services model that blends proprietary technology with human expertise to deliver scalable talent acquisition solutions.

Transaction Terms

The transaction included the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of IQTalent. Under the terms of the agreement, total consideration at closing was approximately $4.7 million, consisting of:

  • $3.2 million in cash, subject to exchange rate changes and a net working capital adjustment; and
  • 1.45 million Caldwell common shares held by David Windley and Tom Milic, who are owners of WinMil and former employees of IQTalent. The shares were valued at approximately $1.5 million, based on a simple average price of $1.05 per Caldwell share over the 20 days prior to closing. The shares have been cancelled by Caldwell, reducing total shares outstanding by approximately 4.9%.

All dollar amounts are presented in Canadian dollars.

Caldwell retains its minority equity interest in the recruitment software company HootRecruit (formerly known as IQRecruit). Caldwell also retains the ability to utilize IQTalent's remaining deferred tax assets to apply against future taxable ordinary income generated by Caldwell in the United States.

Caldwell and WinMil have also entered into a two-year referral agreement to connect clients with the firms' complementary executive search and recruiting services.

Caldwell's Board of Directors will evaluate the use of the cash proceeds as part of its capital allocation planning and expects to provide an update with the release of Caldwell's next quarterly earnings.

​​About Caldwell

Caldwell is an elite executive search firm trusted by established and growth-focused companies alike. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with clients to design and build extraordinary leadership teams. Our partners don't just place executives-they challenge assumptions, enable strategy, and prioritize long-term fit. Built on repeat clients and referrals, Caldwell delivers clarity and results without arrogance or shortcuts. Our suite of services includes executive and board level search, as well as talent strategy and assessment tools that help organizations hire the right people, then manage and inspire them to achieve maximum business results. For clients seeking substance over scale, we're the confident voice that listens-and leads. At Caldwell, our purpose is your mission.

Scottsdale, AZ, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Black Rock Coffee Bar, the Oregon-born boutique coffee chain celebrated for its specialty coffees, teas, smoothies, and signature Fuel® energy drinks, is growing its footprint in California with the opening of a new store in Rancho Cucamonga. 

The store, located at 11370 Fourth St, will officially open its doors on Sunday, October 25th. This opening marks Black Rock’s eighth California location and reinforces the brand’s steady expansion across the state. Guests can enjoy the following specials during opening week: 

  • Sunday, October 25th: $2 Medium Drinks 
  • Monday, October 26th: BOGO Drinks 
  • Tuesday, October 27th: 50% Off a Drink w/ Food Purchase 
  • Wednesday, October 28th: Signature Grand Opening Sticker with a Purchase 
  • Thursday, October 29th: Free T-shirt with a Purchase 
  • Friday, October 30th: $2 Off Any Size Drink 

“California has been an important part of Black Rock’s growth, and we’re excited to expand in the state,” said Mark Davis, CEO of Black Rock Coffee Bar. “We look forward to becoming part of the Rancho Cucamonga community and creating a welcoming place for guests to enjoy their favorite drinks and fuel their day!” 

 

Guests can also take advantage of the Black Rock Rewards app, where every purchase—whether in-store, online, or through the app—earns “bolts” that can be redeemed for free beverages. Recent menu additions, like Black Rock’s protein-packed Egg Bites, are also included in the program. 

 

Black Rock Coffee Bar is beloved for its handcrafted beverages, including the Caramel Blondie, a sweet and creamy signature blend; the Mexican Mocha, a spicy twist with hints of vanilla, almond, and cinnamon; and the Jackhammer, a vanilla mocha with an extra double shot; as well as its in-house developed Fuel energy drink, customizable with over 20 fruit flavors.  These can be enjoyed alongside sweet and savory food items, including the recently launched Grilled Cheese and Pumpkin Blondie Cake Pop. For an extra kick of protein, guests can add Black Rock’s new Protein Cold Foam, Protein Boosted Milk or Protein Boost to their drinks. 

 

In addition to Black Rock menu staples, guests can enjoy limited-time offerings like the Pumpkin Spiced Latte, Pumpkin Blondie, and Pumpkin Spice Cookie Latte with Cookie Butter Cold Foam. The brand’s Fall Remix seasonal drinks are also now available, featuring the Caramel Apple Butter Shaken Espresso, Cinnamon Bun Latte, and Spellbound Berry Fuel, offering a mix of nostalgic and refreshing flavors.  

 

For more information, visit https://br.coffee/ and follow @blackrockcoffeebar on Facebook and Instagram, and @blackrockcoffeeofficial on TikTok for updates on new locations, promotions, and seasonal offerings. 

 

About Black Rock Coffee Bar  

Black Rock Coffee Bar is a national boutique coffee shop that is known for its premium roasted coffees, teas, smoothies and flavorful Fuel® energy drinks. Founded as a family owned and operated business in Oregon in 2008, Black Rock Coffee Bar has grown to over 200 retail locations in seven states. The Black Rock culture prides itself on not only being a positive force for the communities it serves, but also the team members that fuel their locations day in and day out. Johnson is a 27-year veteran of General Dynamics Mission Systems, where she held increasingly senior roles in engineering, engineering management and business leadership across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems, most recently as vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence. She earned bachelor's and master's degrees in computer science and computer systems engineering.

"I am confident that her dynamic leadership, operational rigor and deep commitment to our values and culture will deliver value to our customers, employees and shareholders."

GDIT delivers digital modernization, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and software development solutions to the U.S. federal government, defense, intelligence agencies and other customers. AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) announced today the pilot launch of Vital Farms Free-Range eggs, which are expected to arrive in select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast beginning this week.

This limited test is designed to explore how Vital Farms can reach more households with a high-quality product at a more accessible suggested retail price point of less than $5 per carton, while maintaining its commitment to transparency and animal welfare.

Introducing A New Vital Farms Standard

“Free-range” is one of the most familiar terms in the egg aisle, but the standard itself doesn’t consistently tell consumers what they are actually buying. Compared with many other free-range products, the new Vital Farms Free-Range standard sets a higher bar for animal welfare in several meaningful areas: time outside, better land with living vegetation and shade, and barns designed to make it easier for hens to head outdoors. And like every carton of Vital Farms eggs, each carton can be traced back to the farm where the eggs were laid through the company’s “See The Farm” program.

This new Vital Farms standard for free-range reflects Vital Farms’ commitments to animal care, product quality, and transparency. Vital Farms loves hearing from consumers with questions. Visit vitalfarms.com/contact for details on how to call, text, direct message or write, or visit Vital Farms’ Frequently Asked Questions page to learn more.

Living Within Vital Farms’ Values and Testing Something New

“With Vital Farms Free-Range, we’re testing how we can bring more households a high-quality egg at a more accessible price point, while staying true to who we are and keeping hens’ quality of life front and center,” said Heather Mace, Vital Farms Vice President, Brand. “Our goal is to learn all we can, understand consumer appetite and grow the right way. Reaching more households gives us the opportunity to create more positive impact for our stakeholders while continuing to raise the standards in the egg aisle.”

Vital Farms Free-Range eggs are expected to be available beginning this week at select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast. For more information on where to find Vital Farms eggs, please visit: https://vitalfarms.com/where-to-buy/

ABOUT VITAL FARMS:

Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) is a Certified B Corporation that offers a range of ethically produced foods nationwide. Started on a single farm in Austin, Texas, in 2007, Vital Farms is now a national consumer brand that works with 600 small farms and is the leading U.S. brand of pasture-raised eggs by retail dollar sales. Vital Farms’ ethics are exemplified by its focus on the humane treatment of farm animals and sustainable farming practices. In addition, as a Delaware public benefit corporation, Vital Farms prioritizes the long-term benefits of each of its stakeholders, including farmers and suppliers, customers and consumers, communities and the environment, and crew members and stockholders. Vital Farms’ products, including shell eggs, hard-boiled eggs, and liquid whole eggs, are sold in more than 24,000 stores nationwide. Vital Farms pasture-raised eggs can also be found on menus at hundreds of foodservice operators across the country. For more information, visit https://vitalfarms.com.

Key Terms

restricted stock unitsfinancial
Restricted stock units are a type of company reward where employees are promised shares of stock, but they only fully own these shares after meeting certain conditions, like staying with the company for a set time. They matter because they can become valuable assets and are often used to motivate employees to help the company succeed.
non-qualified stock optionfinancial
A non-qualified stock option (NSO) is a contract that lets an employee or service provider buy company shares at a fixed price for a set period, like a voucher to purchase stock later at today’s price. It matters to investors because exercising NSOs creates ordinary income for the holder and can increase share count, affecting a company’s earnings and ownership mix; think of it as a future sale that can dilute existing shareholders and has immediate tax consequences for the recipient.
nasdaq listing rule 5635(c)(4)regulatory
NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) is a rule that requires a company to get approval from its shareholders before selling a large amount of its shares, usually over 20%. CORYDON, Ind., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- First Capital, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ: FCAP), the holding company for First Harrison Bank (the “Bank”), today reported net income of $5.1 million, or $1.53 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $4.5 million, or $1.34 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Results of Operations for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

Net interest income after provision for credit losses increased $1.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Interest income increased $1.4 million when comparing the two periods due to an increase in the average tax-equivalent yield(1) on interest-earning assets from 4.94% for the third quarter of 2025 to 5.23% for the same period in 2026, in addition to an increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets from $1.20 billion for the third quarter of 2025 to $1.25 billion for the same period in 2026. Interest expense decreased $119,000 when comparing the periods as the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased from 1.66% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to 1.57% for the same period in 2026 while the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities increased from $891.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to $911.5 million for the same period in 2026. As a result of the changes in interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, the tax-equivalent net interest margin(1) increased from 3.71% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to 4.08% for the same period in 2026. Refer to the accompanying average balance sheet for more information regarding changes in the composition of the Company’s balance sheet and resulting yields and costs from the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Based on management’s analysis of the Allowance for Credit Losses (“ACL”) on loans and unfunded loan commitments, the provision for credit losses increased from $150,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to $355,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.   The Bank recognized net charge-offs of $123,000 and $17,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Noninterest income decreased $14,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is primarily due to the Company recognizing a $9,000 loss on equity securities during the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to a gain of $150,000 during the same period in 2025.   That decrease was partially offset by the Company recognizing increases of $92,000 and $57,000 in other income and service charges on deposit accounts, respectively, when comparing the two periods.   The increase in other income was primarily due to the Company recognizing $48,000 and $45,000 in income from its technology investment fund and its renewable energy tax credit investment, respectively, during the quarter.  

Noninterest expenses increased $545,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. This was primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits and other expenses of $585,000 and $75,000, respectively, when comparing the two periods.   The increase in compensation and benefits is due to increases in salary and wages associated with annual cost of living and performance related adjustments as well as increases in the cost of Company-provided health insurance benefits. The increase in other expenses was primarily due to general inflationary pressures and routine pricing increases rather than any specific item. These increases were partially offset by a $148,000 decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses when comparing the two periods. Occupancy and equipment expenses were elevated during the third quarter of 2025 due to disposal losses associated with two of the Bank’s branches, the upgrade of the Company’s call center system, and the demolition of one of the Bank’s branches. None of these were present during the third quarter of 2026.

Income tax expense increased $164,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.4% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 19.2% for the same period in 2025.

Results of Operations for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $14.2 million, or $4.25 per diluted share, compared to net income of $11.5 million, or $3.43 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025.

Net interest income after provision for credit losses increased $4.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Interest income increased $4.6 million when comparing the two periods due to an increase in the average tax-equivalent yield(1) on interest-earning assets from 4.80% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 5.10% for the same period in 2026, in addition to an increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets from $1.19 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $1.24 billion for the same period in 2026. Interest expense decreased $471,000 when comparing the periods as the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased from 1.67% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 1.56% for the same period in 2026 while the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities increased from $886.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $906.8 million for the same period in 2026. As a result of the changes in interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, the tax-equivalent net interest margin(1) increased from 3.55% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 3.96% for the same period in 2026. Refer to the accompanying average balance sheet for more information regarding changes in the composition of the Company’s balance sheet and resulting yields and costs from the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Based on management’s analysis of the ACL on loans and unfunded loan commitments, the provision for credit losses increased from $794,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $1.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Bank recognized net charge-offs of $292,000 and $214,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Noninterest income increased $373,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to the Company recognizing a $261,000 gain on equity securities during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a gain of $127,000 during the same period in 2025. In addition, the Company recognized increases of $110,000, $70,000 and $50,000 in service charges on deposit accounts, other income and ATM and debit card fee income, respectively, when comparing the two periods.   The increase in other income was primarily due to the Company recognizing a $47,000 increase in income from its renewable energy tax credit investment during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, in addition to $48,000 of income from its technology investment fund during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 that the Company did not receive during the same period in 2025. These were partially offset by the Company recognizing a $47,000 gain on the redemption of a bank-owned life insurance policy during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, and no such redemption occurred during the same period in 2026.  

Noninterest expenses increased $1.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. This was primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits, other expenses, professional services, and advertising expenses of $1.1 million, $253,000, $132,000 and $92,000, respectively, when comparing the two periods. The increase in compensation and benefits is due to increases in salary and wages associated with annual cost of living and performance related adjustments as well as increases in the cost of Company-provided health insurance benefits. The increase in other expenses is primarily due to a $70,000 increase in consumer fraud losses and general inflationary pressures and routine pricing increases during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025.   The increase in professional services is due to increased consulting fees. The increase in advertising expenses is related to various new marketing campaigns undertaken during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses of $110,000 due to a reduction in building maintenance expenses.

Income tax expense increased $919,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.8% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 18.4% for the same period in 2025. The increase in the Company’s effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 reflects a higher proportion of net income being subject to taxation compared to the same period last year.

Comparison of Financial Condition at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025

Total assets were $1.27 billion at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Net loans receivable and other assets increased $20.9 million and $2.2 million, respectively, from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. These increases were partially offset by a decrease of $22.5 million in available for sale securities when comparing the two periods. Deposits increased $6.4 million from $1.12 billion at December 31, 2025 to $1.13 billion at September 30, 2026. Nonperforming assets (consisting of nonaccrual loans, accruing loans 90 days or more past due, and foreclosed real estate) increased from $4.4 million at December 31, 2025 to $5.5 million at September 30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the nonaccrual classification of a non-owner occupied commercial real estate loan.

BETHESDA, Md., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Elme Communities (“Elme” or the “Company”) today announced that the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) has exercised its discretionary authority in accordance with Section 802.01D of the NYSE Listed Company Manual to commence proceedings to delist Elme’s common shares of beneficial interest (the “Common Shares”) from the NYSE due to “abnormally low selling price” levels. The NYSE also immediately suspended trading of the Common Shares. Given the Company’s previously adopted Plan of Sale and Liquidation (as defined below), Elme does not intend to appeal the NYSE’s determination, and, therefore, it is expected that the Common Shares will be delisted. 

The Company anticipates the Common Shares will commence trading over-the-counter (“OTC”) on Monday, October 26, 2026 under the symbol “ELMES”. There can be no assurance regarding the development or maintenance of an active OTC trading market or the liquidity of any such market. Investors are cautioned that trading securities OTC is more limited and subject to different restrictions than trading securities listed on a national securities exchange and are advised to consult their own brokers or advisors.

Anticipated Timing of Establishment of a Liquidating Trust and Company Dissolution

As previously disclosed, in accordance with the Plan of Sale and Liquidation approved by the Board of Trustees (the “Board”) on July 30, 2025 and by the shareholders of the Company on October 30, 2025 (the “Plan of Sale and Liquidation”), it is the Company’s continued intention to terminate its existence by voluntary dissolution effective November 6, 2026 (the “Effective Time”), which will occur following the NYSE’s delisting of our Common Shares. In addition, as previously disclosed, the Company expects that its share transfer books will close at the close of business (Eastern Time) on November 5, 2026.

Prior to the Effective Time, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets and liabilities to a Maryland liquidating trust (the “Liquidating Trust”). The purpose of the Liquidating Trust will be to liquidate the remaining assets (which are expected to consist primarily of the net cash proceeds from property sales) of the Liquidating Trust and distribute the amounts remaining in the Liquidating Trust, if any, after satisfaction of all remaining liabilities (including any additional liabilities, costs and expenses that may arise during the wind-down process) to the holders of the beneficial interests of the Liquidating Trust (the “Beneficial Interests”) upon completion of the wind-down process and in connection with termination of the Liquidating Trust. All of the Beneficial Interests will be held by the shareholders of the Company, with each shareholder of the Company being deemed automatically to have received and hold a percentage of Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust corresponding to such shareholder’s percentage ownership in the Company as of the close of business on the last day of trading of the Common Shares. Shareholders of the Company will not be required to take any action to receive Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust. The actual amount and timing of payment of any additional liquidating distribution(s) from the Liquidating Trust will be determined by the trustee of the Liquidating Trust in their sole discretion. As previously disclosed, the Company expects FTI Consulting, Inc. to be retained to provide services in connection with completing the wind-down process, including the services of a liquidating trustee to serve as trustee of the Liquidating Trust.

Following the transfer of the Company’s assets and liabilities to the Liquidating Trust, subject to certain exceptions related to transfer by will, intestate succession or operation of law, Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust will not be transferable, nor will holders of Beneficial Interests have authority or power to sell or in any other manner dispose of their Beneficial Interests. The Beneficial Interests will not trade on the NYSE, or any other exchange or OTC. Simultaneously, all of the outstanding Common Shares and certificates representing Common Shares will be automatically cancelled and will thereafter no longer be deemed outstanding. The rights of holders of Beneficial Interests will not be represented by any form of certificate or other instrument.

For a discussion of the tax consequences of the transfer of the Company’s assets to the Liquidating Trust and the deemed distribution of the Beneficial Interests to the shareholders, please see “Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences - Tax Consequences of the Liquidating Trust” beginning on page 76 of the definitive proxy statement filed by the Company with the SEC on September 24, 2025 for the special meeting of shareholders held on October 30, 2025, which is available free of charge through the website maintained by the SEC at http://www.sec.gov or the Company’s website at www.elmecommunities.com. You are urged to consult your own tax advisor to determine the particular tax consequences to you of the transfer of the Company’s assets to the Liquidating Trust and the deemed distribution of Beneficial Interests to the shareholders, including the applicability and effect of any U.S. federal, state and local and foreign tax laws.

Based on guidance previously provided by the SEC in similar circumstances, assuming the Company terminates its existence as described above, the Company anticipates that the Liquidating Trust will be required to file only annual reports on Form 10-K (using the SEC file number of the Company) containing unaudited financial statements, as well as current reports on Form 8-K (also filed using the SEC file number of the Company).

About Elme Communities

Elme Communities is a Maryland real estate investment trust. Elme, in accordance with and as anticipated by the Plan of Sale and Liquidation, expects to dissolve on November 6, 2026. Prior to the Company’s dissolution, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets to Elme Communities Liquidating Trust for the benefit of holders of the Common Shares in accordance with and as anticipated by the Plan of Sale and Liquidation.

Research Will Use Lunit’s AI-powered Pathology Platform to Analyze H&E Whole-Slide Images and Generate Scalable Insights into Tumor Microenvironment Biology

MIAMI & SEOUL, South Korea--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Summit Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: SMMT) and Lunit Inc. (KRX: 328130) today announced a research agreement to evaluate the use of Lunit SCOPE IO, Lunit’s AI-powered pathology platform, for tumor microenvironment analysis in support of Summit’s immuno-oncology development programs with ivonescimab.

The effort will focus on applying Lunit SCOPE IO to hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) whole-slide images to characterize tumor microenvironment features. The companies aim to explore how AI-powered pathology analysis can support biomarker discovery, patient stratification or selection, and a deeper biological understanding of response to ivonescimab therapies.

Summit is developing ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class investigational PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, in several solid tumors. Lunit SCOPE IO is designed to support immuno-oncology research and biomarker development through AI-powered analysis of H&E slides, enabling scalable assessment of tumor microenvironment features without requiring additional stains or assays.

“Understanding the tumor microenvironment is increasingly important as immuno-oncology moves beyond single-axis checkpoint inhibition toward more complex mechanisms and combinations,” said Allen Yang, MD, PhD, Chief Research and Development Strategy Officer of Summit. “We are pleased to work with Lunit to explore how AI-powered pathology can help generate deeper, more scalable insights from routine tissue samples and inform the continued development of ivonescimab.”

“Summit is at the forefront of next-generation immuno-oncology development, and we are excited to support its efforts with Lunit SCOPE IO,” said Brandon Suh, Lunit CEO. “By extracting quantitative, spatially resolved immune and tumor microenvironment features from standard H&E slides, we believe SCOPE IO can help biopharma partners better understand which patients may benefit from immuno-oncology therapies and why.”

This agreement reflects the growing importance of computational pathology in oncology drug development. Routine H&E slides contain rich information about tumor architecture, immune infiltration, stromal organization, and spatial interactions within the tumor microenvironment. However, traditional manual assessment can be difficult to scale and may not fully capture the quantitative and spatial complexity of the tumor-immune interface. AI-powered analysis offers the potential to convert these routinely generated pathology images into reproducible, high-dimensional biomarker data.

The companies expect the work to generate tumor microenvironment insights that may inform future translational research, exploratory biomarker strategies, and clinical development planning. No clinical outcome data are being announced as part of this release.

Lunit SCOPE products are for research use only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures or decisions.

About Ivonescimab

Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit’s license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit’s license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.

This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab’s specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of ivonescimab’s design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.

Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.

There are currently 17 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, five of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, two of which are studies sponsored by cooperative groups, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC (HARMONi, HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7) and expanded its sponsored Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC; HARMONi-GI3) and urothelial carcinoma (bladder cancer; HARMONi-GU1). The two cooperative studies are in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; ILLUMINE) and biliary tract cancer (BTC; EA2251).

Five Phase III ivonescimab clinical trials have read out to date, all five with positive data. Four of these five studies are in NSCLC and one is in BTC. In addition to Summit’s positive HARMONi study in NSCLC, Akeso has had positive read-outs in four single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6 (each in NSCLC), and HARMONi-GI1 (in BTC) for ivonescimab, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in all four studies from China.

Akeso is actively conducting additional Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC and biliary-tract cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.

About Lunit Inc.

Founded in 2013, Lunit (KRX: 328130) is a global leader on a mission to conquer cancer through AI. Key Terms

pd-1medical
PD-1 is a protein found on certain immune cells that acts like a brake, signaling the immune system to slow down and avoid damaging healthy tissue. Drugs that block PD-1 release that brake so immune cells can better attack cancer cells; because such therapies can produce large clinical benefits, regulatory approvals, trial outcomes, pricing and market uptake for PD-1 drugs can materially affect a drugmaker’s prospects and investor returns.
vegfmedical
Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is a naturally occurring protein that signals the body to grow new blood vessels, like a fertilizer prompts plants to sprout. It matters to investors because drugs that block or mimic VEGF can dramatically change outcomes for cancers and eye diseases, making them major drivers of clinical trial results, regulatory approvals, market value and future revenue potential for biopharma companies.
bispecific antibodymedical
A bispecific antibody is a specially designed protein that can attach to two different targets at the same time. Think of it as a custom-made connector that brings two things together—such as a disease cell and an immune system component—helping the body fight illnesses more effectively. For investors, understanding bispecific antibodies is important because they represent innovative therapies that could lead to new treatments and potentially lucrative market opportunities.
